summary: Seek bounded message pages through body-free temporal selectors

replay.detail: Opening an older database backfills local message selector headers from current message projections and retained canonical claims in short, resumable chunks before readers are served. Starting a backfill invalidates existing page cuts. No authoritative claim replay or body-copy inventory is introduced; ordinary pages fold only selected message bodies.

schema.detail: Adds local_client_message_selectors_v1: a body-free header/pending/quarantine table with twenty-two indexes and seven source-change triggers, completed-cut and resumable backfill/fold markers. Five retained-cut eligibility indexes contain retired headers only; historical open pages combine bounded live and retired index branches, avoiding duplicate historical-index writes on ordinary sends. The seventh trigger queues full folds/quarantine for message repairs and repaired replacement reselections. local_client_message_fold_batches stores only batch IDs/legacy wire-position prefix counts and skips scratch persistence for single-row completed prefixes. local_client_message_publications stores retention cohorts only when a retirement needs its first covering publication, plus the initial bootstrap cohort; cut advances without retirement add no cohort. Retired headers remain until their first covering publication is older than the cursor lifetime; bounded cohort cleanup preserves the latest stored cohort. The fold marker retains canonical keys and selection scalars, never content or attachments. Suspended full folds retain append progress/extend their cut; destructive epoch changes or newly dirty metadata-only bases restart them. Runtime::before_commit performs the sole selector fold at each managed outer transaction boundary, for both batched and lent writers, and composes before the source adapter finalizer. Append/apply/replay helpers no longer reset the allowance by folding eagerly. One transaction gets at most 64 claim/prefix rows and 16 subjects with a cooperative 10 ms work budget; selector/scratch cleanup is bounded. A weakly owned daemon worker drains remaining work in independent writer loans; idle checks do not borrow/commit the writer, and last-task completion wakes readers/events. Malformed desired JSON skips the subject's header, warns and increments a local counter. Desired deletion uses fixed-size indexed old/new global and recipient winner seeks rather than rewriting or inventorying an entire reminder group. A 4,096-native-member/97-declaration regression measures at most nine selector-row mutations per declaration deletion, preserves unrelated members and checks bulk owner deletion plus bounded durable draining. Final reversed-order 128-send/128-close real-append bursts measured send p95 deltas of +0.860/+0.710 ms and close p95 deltas of +0.604/+1.127 ms. Send WAL was 125,853.375 to 189,101.8125 bytes per commit (+50.26%); close WAL was 112,366.8125 to 226,374.9375 bytes per commit (+101.46%). Additional WAL per 128-commit burst was 8,095,800 bytes for sends and 14,593,040 bytes for closes. Write measurements disable automatic checkpoints to isolate WAL cost and retain production FULL synchronous commits. Page p95 ranges across limit-20 first/next filter cases were 5.044-5.772 ms at 128 messages, 5.456-6.313 ms at 1,280 and 5.772-6.815 ms at 12,800 (422,400 claims). Across five closed-heavy runs, open-page p95 ranged from 0.513 to 0.952 ms. Cursor epochs also fence repaired replacement reselections; earlier body-version tables/triggers are removed idempotently. Registry and replication compatibility digests, authoritative claims and claim formats are unchanged.

rules.detail: Canonical claim-log checkpoint rules, the schema registry digest and shared projection digests are unchanged. SQLite WAL checkpoint scheduling during startup backfill and explicit selector rebuild changes as described under downtime; it is distinct from canonical checkpoints. Deletion or repair that destroys a retained message cut, or a selector backfill start, invalidates that traversal instead of returning a partial successful page.

compatibility.detail: Message JSON, recipient/actor filters, ordering, reminder selection and snapshot-consistent traversal are preserved. Pending selector tasks are invisible; ordinary incomplete maintenance serves and pins the last fully published frontier. Desired-projection deletion immediately clears declaration-derived fields and eligibility, expires existing cursors and appears on fresh pages before reconciliation completes; retained intent.desired claims do not restore deleted fields. Its synchronous selector mutations are confined to the affected subject and old/new global and recipient winners; indexed LIMIT 1 seeks preserve canonical winner ordering and unrelated reminder-group members. Native reminder metadata and a preexisting pending row's old recipient survive deletion. Destructive claim update/delete, message repair and repaired replacement reselection expire old cursors and insert one durable born_index=-2 quarantine marker per subject; fresh pages temporarily omit that subject until replacement reconciles and its cut is published. The desired-projection shortcut requires an indexed subject/kind check proving no declaration after the requested cut. Continuations bind exact store cut, snapshot, filters, limit, position and expiry. Tampered, expired, evicted, restarted or deletion-invalidated cursors return HTTP 410/page-cursor-expired. Delivery presence remains live on each page while delivery age retains the first request time.

downtime.detail: Initial selector backfill runs at startup in resumable clear, subject-queue and claim-row-bounded pending phases; startup pages wait for the completed frontier. Startup and explicit rebuild share a driver that disables automatic WAL checkpoints during chunking, runs a PASSIVE checkpoint outside all transactions even when the incoming automatic policy was already disabled, and restores that policy on success or error. The migration benchmark preserves the production automatic policy rather than disabling it in its IO setup. On a fresh temporary copy of a checkpointed 118,390-claim, 9,712-message, 1.65-GiB database, full Store open took 12.310 s. Startup backfill used 1,250 transactions, at most 16 subjects and 64 claim/prefix rows per transaction, with 5.666 s chunk-driver total and longest commit-inclusive transaction 19.009 ms (10.076 ms work, 8.931 ms COMMIT); its outside-transaction checkpoint took 32.324 ms. Explicit rebuild used 1,401 transactions with the same bounds, 6.101 s chunk-driver total and 6.136 s including its 33.488 ms outside-transaction checkpoint; longest commit-inclusive transaction was 18.311 ms (9.139 ms work, 9.170 ms COMMIT). Both migration-copy gates passed the 100 ms threshold. Populated reopen took 32.955 ms with zero backfill transactions. Five fresh closed-heavy runs were traced with fsync/fdatasync/pwrite64 and independent longest-COMMIT timing. Their longest COMMITs were 4.693, 5.617, 8.567, 6.554 and 5.218 ms (minimum 4.693, median 5.617, maximum 8.567 ms); longest commit-inclusive transactions were 12.211, 10.611, 13.246, 12.764 and 10.900 ms, with no observed 100 ms violation across 8,140 chunk transactions. During those precise longest-COMMIT intervals, WAL fsync took 0.744, 4.060, 6.637, 4.511 and 0.617 ms. The three largest COMMITs were dominated by those measured WAL fsync waits; post-COMMIT WAL lengths ranged from 83,800,832 to 184,666,672 bytes. Automatic checkpoints were disabled during chunks and the outside-transaction PASSIVE checkpoint took 325.531-422.898 ms. Test-only timing and file-length instrumentation does not change production durability. The earlier 330.532 ms synthetic transaction (0.602 ms work, 329.929 ms COMMIT) did not recur in these five runs; its untraced cause remains unestablished. These repeated passing observations do not erase that outlier or prove the mandatory universal 100 ms wall-time requirement. The migration source was read-only and all writes went to fresh temporary copies. Checkpoint cost is included in the full run; these API-only Store measurements are not live-daemon restart-to-API or rollout downtime proofs.

manual.detail: No manual migration, identity change or claim-log maintenance is required. Clients restart pagination on page-cursor-expired.

recovery.detail: Binary swap-back cannot restore issued in-memory cursor metadata; clients restart traversals. The authoritative claim log remains intact and older claim-based readers continue to work. A runtime that reintroduces the removed local body version store must recreate and seed it from claims.
